questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer:
Several aspects were crucial, including: 
1) English-speaking country/city --> possible for me to improve both my written and spoken English 
2) A strong/good reputation --> the University of Edinburgh is known for being welcoming to international students; it offers the opportunity to meet other exchange students from around the world (possible to expand my international network)
3) The vibe of the city !! Very cosy and chill city to be in during fall

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
The city is quite expensive to live in, and finding housing was challenging. 
Furthermore, I did not get the courses I had initially hoped for + the teaching was different from back home (more opinion-based than factual; very different from the law courses at KU)

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Easy. It's easy to reach out to UoE and their visiting student office with any questions + the UoE homepage has lots on information about housing, the courses etc.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: The university assisted me in securing student accommodation after I had arrived in the city, despite the fact that I had technically missed the application deadline. As I was dissatisfied with the private accommodation I was staying in, they were understanding and supportive and helped me find a room within 24 hours.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I lived in a flat with four other girls, where we had our own rooms. We, however, had a bathroom, two toilets and a kitchen to share.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: I lived in self-catered student accommodation, though it was possible to apply for catered accommodation.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: My flatmates were quite young, as the only ones living in student accommodation are either other exchange students or first-year students.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The housing was expensive, even though the facilities were not particularly good; the rooms had mould, and the toilets were occasionally problematic.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: They email you instructions on how to check in, and it’s easy to contact them if you have any questions about the process.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: See above. They also have lots of information on their homepage.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: They operate on a first-come, first-served basis, which is why I didn’t get the courses I initially wanted. Changing courses was a lengthy process once I had already started attending classes, but I managed to switch to two new courses. However, I know that others were not as fortunate as I was. There are limited spots in several of the more popular courses for exchange students, and this could be communicated more clearly in the course offerings.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be quick to submit the courses you want when you receive the email from the university instructing you to do so. Make sure to familiarize yourself with the different courses and their requirements beforehand. I only chose courses that were assessed through coursework, so I didn’t have any written or oral exams. I was very happy with this choice, as it made my semester much easier.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: See below.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I only took honours courses, which are attended only by third- and fourth-year students. As a result, the level was slightly higher. However, I wasn’t particularly challenged by the content itself—my main challenge was adapting to the different teaching style. See below.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There was a greater emphasis on critically engaging with the law and expressing our own opinions on topics such as EU law and various legislations. This differed from KU, where the focus is on being presented with facts and legal principles and then connecting them. At UoE, the approach was more discussion-based and encouraged innovation (at least in the courses I took). For instance, in Strategic Decision Making, I had to develop my own project, and in EU Law, I was required to pose a critical question about the EU and respond to it with my own perspective. In other words, there was a strong focus on formulating a clear "main argument."

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
1) Strategic Decision Making: Game Theory and the Law 
2) Human Rights Honours 
3) EU Law Honours: Foundations

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The Human Rights Honours course was great; the topics covered were very interesting, and the exam consisted of a 4000-word essay on one of the topics studied.

questions.answer:
Housing was more expensive than expected. 
However, books are online making it unnecessary to buy them. 
Food is cheaper; ate out a lot instead of making food at home (hence the value at personal spending).

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: So many clubs and societies to join! Great way to meet other people as well.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
Sport-clubs. 
There was a Scandi-society where I attended some of their events as well; great way to be able to speak danish :)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go out to the Highlands! I can't recommend it enough.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Edinburgh is not that different from Denmark.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Go to pubs or join the societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: How relaxed and kind people were. It's a "slow" city; almost empty on Sundays as well :)

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) Take time to find accommodation; consider teaming up with other Danes who are also going to the city (for example, through the Facebook group that is set up)
2) Be open to meet other people (not only other Danes !)
3) Remember to relax; you also bring your everyday life with you, so don’t try to have plans every single day.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: See above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I met, and the memories we have together now.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The housing-situation! Don't underestimate it.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
